decisions.reason: This modular plant concept builds directly on the firm's core recycling-system knowledge and already showed strong customer value through reported cost savings, so the firm has both the absorptive capacity and the market signal to keep improving it.

As a mobile slow-speed shredder very close to the established portfolio, it fits existing engineering, service and telematics capabilities well, making continued refinement more likely than withdrawal.

Because this modular plant concept is both closely related to the firm's knowledge base and presented as a flagship direction, management would strongly prefer to scale and learn from it rather than remove it.

The mobile trommel screen is adjacent to the core offer and therefore within the firm's absorptive capacity, but with less visible standout evidence than the lead concepts its withdrawal risk remains somewhat higher while still low.

This new slow-speed shredder line is highly related to the firm's existing mobile processing equipment and can be improved through in-house R&D, field feedback and university-linked learning, so it is likely to be retained.

The mobile spiral shaft screen line builds on established screening and materials-processing know-how, and in a growing firm with active R&D the likely response is iteration and portfolio development rather than early exit.
